title: Hating to leave the European band; playing I Can't Stop Loving You his own way
summary: Davenport enjoyed two weeks with the band and contrasts it with playing set arrangements with Basie and Ray Charles.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You know, I hated to leave those guys. See, I played with them two weeks. And I hated to leave. They hated for me to leave.
Did you feel comfortable with them? Yes.

You know, I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated them so many years. I do it my way. You do it your way. And it doesn't go that way. If they were playing with any major band, you have to play the way you want. The arrangement called. Like when I was playing with Carl Basie. He had a hit arrangement on. I mean a hit record on. I said, I can't stop loving you. I played with Ray Charles for two years before that. He had also had a hit record on I Can't Stop Loving You. Now I suppose I had gotten to the calm base and said, well look, I'm a player I Can't Stop Loving You like that. I played it like this when I was with Ray Charles.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I suppose you had a first base when you said, well you guys play baseball. You're well played my way. But what happened to the team? It's the same thing to me.
